project.name: semanticd-dashboard
project.description: The SIF console web UI. A two-product Vite package: one shared src/ tree built into two apps (sif and codewall) selected by Vite --mode.

nodes.name: DemoContext.tsx
nodes.summary: React context that holds the demo switch for the tab, resolving `?demo=1` once on mount and exposing the flag plus a setter to every panel. With no provider above it the context yields a permanently-off state rather than throwing, so adding a demo panel can never crash or alter a page that is not in demo mode.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a lazy `useState` initialiser so the URL parameter is resolved exactly once per mount; re-running it on every location change would let a later link carrying `?demo=0` silently flip the switch.

nodes.name: clock.ts
nodes.summary: Derives every demo timestamp from `Date.now()` at render time, taking a minutes-ago offset instead of a stored literal date. Keeps fixtures from ageing into obviously stale timestamps, and stays free of randomness so a rehearsed demo shows the same numbers on the night.

nodes.name: loaders.ts
nodes.summary: The only module that names a demo fixture, wrapping each one in a dynamic `import()` so the invented numbers live in their own chunk and are fetched only when a panel actually asks. A guard test fails the build on any static import from `fixtures/`, which is the other half of that containment.
nodes.languageNotes: Each loader is a dynamic `import().then(m => m.x)` arrow — the module boundary is what keeps fixture code out of the bundle while the switch is off.

nodes.name: mode.ts
nodes.summary: The demo switch itself: reads and writes a single `sessionStorage` token, never localStorage, a cookie, a build flag or an environment variable, and resolves `?demo=1` on page load. Every failure path returns off, so a storage exception or a stray value can never half-enable invented data for a real customer.
nodes.languageNotes: Only the exact string `on` counts as consent, and turning the switch off removes the key rather than writing a falsy string — so the reader has exactly one state to recognise.

nodes.name: useDemoQuery.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Query wrapper that loads a demo fixture only while the switch is on, using `enabled` so the loader's dynamic import never runs in the off state and the fixture chunk never reaches the browser. Adds a small artificial latency so panels show the same skeleton as real ones, and caches forever since a fixture is a constant.

nodes.name: NotFound.tsx
nodes.summary: Catch-all route rendered for any path the router does not recognise, echoing the attempted path and linking back to Overview. Replaces the previously-blank main region that made a stale bookmark look like a broken build after the section restructure moved every page.

nodes.name: Reports.tsx
nodes.summary: Placeholder screen for the Reports section, which is genuinely undesigned. Says so plainly and routes the reader to Activity › Audit, which carries the same ground today — the empty-state rule applied to a whole page rather than inventing content.

nodes.name: GovernanceSection.tsx
nodes.summary: Groups the three governance demo panels into one block appended to the end of Guardrails › Policies, returning null when the switch is off so the page reads exactly as it does in production. Appended rather than interleaved, because a demo panel between two real ones would leave a gap when it vanished.

nodes.name: NetworkOverview.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only Network screen composing the counters, the protocol and counterparty summaries, and the lane and counterparty tables. Renders NotFound with the switch off, so a route that cannot show anything does not exist rather than appearing broken.

nodes.name: Overview.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only four-quadrant estate summary, deliberately given its own route rather than placed on Home so the attention queue there is not replaced by a status dashboard. Each quadrant links through to the screen it summarises; NotFound with the switch off.

nodes.name: DemoProvider
nodes.summary: Provider that resolves the demo switch once from the URL or session storage and exposes it with a setter that reads storage back after writing, so the UI never claims the switch moved when the write was refused.

nodes.name: useDemoMode
nodes.summary: Hook returning the tab's demo state, falling back to a permanently-off value when no provider is mounted rather than throwing and taking the whole app down with one panel.

nodes.name: at
nodes.summary: Returns the Date `minutes` before now — the base every other demo timestamp is derived from.

nodes.name: clockTime
nodes.summary: Formats a minutes-ago offset as a zero-padded 24-hour clock string such as `14:07`, for chart and table labels.

nodes.name: ago
nodes.summary: Renders a minutes-ago offset as a human age — `just now`, `4 min`, `2 h`, `3 d`. Avoids `0 min`, which reads as a bug on a screen built to look live.

nodes.name: loadGovernance
nodes.summary: Dynamically imports the governance fixture chunk and returns its `governance` export, so policy demo data is fetched only when a governance panel in demo mode asks for it.

nodes.name: loadPayments
nodes.summary: Dynamically imports the payments fixture chunk and returns its `payments` export, keeping invented transaction data out of the bundle until a payments panel asks.

nodes.name: loadNetwork
nodes.summary: Dynamically imports the network fixture chunk and returns its `network` export, used by the lane, protocol-mix and counterparty panels.

nodes.name: loadCapsules
nodes.summary: Dynamically imports the capsules fixture chunk and returns its `capsules` export, used by the edge-capsule attestation panel.

nodes.name: isDemoOn
nodes.summary: Reads the demo switch from session storage, matching only the exact consent token and returning false on any exception, so a private window or a browser blocking site data reads as off.

nodes.name: setDemoMode
nodes.summary: Writes or removes the session-storage token for the demo switch, swallowing storage failures so the switch simply stays where it was — which, absent a successful write, is off.

nodes.name: resolveDemoMode
nodes.summary: Resolves the switch for a page load: `?demo=1` turns it on and persists it so the mode survives navigation, any other explicit `demo` value turns it off, and an absent parameter defers to whatever the tab already holds.

nodes.name: useDemoQuery
nodes.summary: Runs a fixture loader through TanStack Query gated on the demo switch — `enabled` is the load-bearing option that stops the dynamic import running at all when off. Adds 150 ms of fake latency and disables refetching so a panel never repaints mid-demo.

nodes.name: NotFound

nodes.name: PaymentsOverview.tsx

nodes.summary: Demo-only panel showing how much of its monthly cap each agent has spent, as a meter against the total. Sorted by proportion spent rather than amount, so an agent at 87% of a small cap outranks one at 47% of a large one.
nodes.languageNotes: The alert state comes from the fixture rather than a threshold computed in the component — inventing a rule for "close to the cap" would be a policy decision dressed up as a colour.

nodes.name: ApprovalsQueue.tsx

nodes.name: AstridCapsules.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only panel listing the enforcement capsules deployed at the edge and whether each is attested, appended to Fleet › System because attestation is infrastructure health. Sorted so anything unattested comes first, since that is the only row worth looking at.

nodes.name: AuditLedger.tsx

nodes.name: CashFlow.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only 24-hour cash-flow chart plotting money out against money in on one axis and one maximum, because the question is the ratio rather than the absolute figure the counters above already give.

nodes.name: Counterparties.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only table of everyone on the other end of an open lane — kind, location, volume and last-seen age. Renders nothing when the demo switch is off.

nodes.name: CounterpartyTypes.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only donut breaking counterparties down by kind — a composition question rather than a ranking one. Uses one hue at descending weight instead of a hue per kind, so the chart does not read as scoring vendors against banks.
nodes.languageNotes: One sorted array feeds both the ring and the legend; sorting them separately would pair a swatch with the wrong label and nothing would look broken.

nodes.name: DecisionsByCategory.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only panel rendering allow / review / deny counts per policy category as a stacked bar per row, so six rows of three numbers become a shape read at a glance. Allow is deliberately neutral rather than green — an allowed request is the ordinary outcome, not an achievement.
nodes.languageNotes: The only reference to a fixture module outside `loaders.ts` is a type-only `import type` of `DecisionRow`, which TypeScript erases at build — the runtime containment of fixture data is unaffected.

nodes.name: GovernanceKpis.tsx

nodes.name: OpenLanes.tsx

nodes.name: ProtocolMix.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only 24-hour breakdown of which protocols carried the traffic, deriving each share from the crossing count at render rather than storing both. A fixture where the bar and the number can drift apart is one that will eventually lie in a demo.

nodes.name: Quadrants.tsx
nodes.summary: The four cards of the demo Overview screen kept in one file because they are one composition — same shape, same rhythm, each a headline figure plus a qualifier plus a link into the screen behind it. Security deliberately reads the real stats summary that Home and Threats use, so three quadrants are invented and one is true.
nodes.languageNotes: Four named exports rather than a default: the components are siblings of equal weight, and splitting them across four files would let a set that must read as one drift apart.

nodes.name: RailBalances.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only table of what sits on each payment rail. Keeps a disabled rail on the list rather than filtering it out, so "why can we not pay in USDC" is a question the screen answers instead of one it creates.

nodes.name: TopVendors.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only ranking of where the money went, biggest first, with each bar measured against the largest vendor rather than the total — against the total, one dominant vendor would leave the rest as unreadable slivers.

nodes.name: Transactions.tsx
nodes.summary: Demo-only table of every payment an agent made or took, as one time-sorted list rather than separate in and out tables — the sign carries the direction, and what a reader wants is what just happened. Status tone maps denied to danger and held or pending to caution, since those are waiting on a person rather than failures.
nodes.languageNotes: The only reference to a fixture module outside `loaders.ts` is a type-only `import type` of `Transaction`, which TypeScript erases at build, so the runtime containment of fixture data still holds.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: The dashboard's shared UI vocabulary as a single barrel — cards, modals, stats, pills, charts, pagination, navigation, status and colour helpers. Pages import from here and never from the individual modules, so the design-system surface stays one thing.
nodes.languageNotes: Re-exports values and types in paired statements (`export { X }` plus `export type { XProps }`), which keeps the barrel compatible with TypeScript's isolated-modules build.

nodes.name: client.ts
nodes.summary: The single HTTP client for the SIF `/manage` control-plane API: an authenticated fetch pipeline (single 401 retry against the refresh token, 403 surfaced as a dismissible RBAC notice) plus ~80 thin typed wrappers, one per backend route.
nodes.languageNotes: All routes are children of a single `MANAGE_BASE = "/manage"` prefix; `requestUrl` is split out from `request` so the sibling `/platform` and unauthenticated `/api` routes can share the same pipeline.

nodes.name: queries.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Query layer wrapping the API client: declares every cache key once, exposes ~50 typed query and mutation hooks, and invalidates precisely (with optimistic rollback on the toggles) so pages hold no server state of their own.
nodes.languageNotes: Cache keys are declared as const key factories (`rulesetKeys`, `policyKeys`, `ruleLibraryKey`) rather than string-built at call sites, which is what makes invalidation targetable.

nodes.name: threats.ts
nodes.summary: Normalizes audit entries into threat events, absorbing the wire-shape drift the server has emitted across versions (bare `detections` array vs `{risk_score, items}` wrapper, stored vs derived risk score).
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately placed in the API layer rather than the page: it is a wire-compatibility concern, and its tests pin both historical shapes.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: The TypeScript mirror of the Rust backend wire contract — policies, rulesets, rules, match specs, API keys, agent classes, audit entries, users, capabilities, tenants and their responses.
nodes.languageNotes: Type-only module (one value export, the `PolicyMode` union helper); everything else is `interface`/`type`, so it erases entirely at build time.

nodes.name: capabilities.ts
nodes.summary: RBAC capability gating for the UI: the compile-time capability union, a `can()` predicate, a React context provider seeded from `GET /manage/auth/me`, and a `RequireCapability` guard.
nodes.languageNotes: Gating fails closed — an absent capability means the action is unavailable — and the comment is explicit that the server remains the sole enforcement point.

nodes.name: fetchWithAuth
nodes.summary: Sends an authenticated request and, on a 401, renews the access token from the refresh token exactly once before replaying it — a second 401 on a fresh token is a real refusal, not an expiry.

nodes.name: handleForbidden
nodes.summary: Turns a 403 body into a dismissible RBAC notice, preferring the server's own `ManageError.message` (e.g. "Cannot delete the last admin user") over generic copy.

nodes.name: requestUrl
nodes.summary: The full request pipeline against an already-formed URL: JSON headers, 403 handling, ApiError on failure, JSON body on success. Split out from `request` so `/platform` routes can reuse it.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: The primary call surface every `/manage` wrapper goes through — prefixes `MANAGE_BASE` and delegates to `requestUrl`.

nodes.name: extractServerMessage
nodes.summary: Pulls the human-readable refusal out of a `ManageError` body, falling back to the raw body and then to a status summary.

nodes.name: serverMessage
nodes.summary: Extracts the server's own words from a thrown error so UI callers can show them, with a caller-supplied fallback for an empty body.

nodes.name: exportPolicyYaml
nodes.summary: Fetches a policy's canonical YAML as text rather than JSON, backing the "Download YAML" action so the result can be committed to `policies/`.

nodes.name: createApiKey
nodes.summary: Creates an API key and returns the one-time plaintext secret alongside the stored record.

nodes.name: rotateApiKey
nodes.summary: Rotates an API key with an optional grace period during which the old secret still authenticates.

nodes.name: createAgentClass
nodes.summary: Creates an agent class with its slug, description and attached policy set.

nodes.name: submitFeedback
nodes.summary: Writes an analyst feedback row (false positive / false negative / expected change) against a request id.

nodes.name: logout
nodes.summary: Best-effort server-side session revocation on sign-out: deliberately a bare keepalive fetch, not `request()`, so a failure neither throws nor emits a spurious "session expired" mid sign-out, and it waits on an in-flight refresh so the replacement session is the one revoked.

nodes.name: exportReceipts
nodes.summary: Downloads the receipts export for a query window as a file body rather than JSON.

nodes.name: createTenant
nodes.summary: Creates a tenant through the `/platform` sibling routes, which live outside the `/manage` prefix.

nodes.name: ApiError
nodes.summary: Error carrying the HTTP status and raw response body, with its message set to the server's own words via `extractServerMessage`.

nodes.name: PUT /manage/rulesets/{id}/rules
nodes.summary: Ruleset membership: list the rules in a ruleset, create a rule into it, and replace the whole ordered membership set in one PUT.

nodes.summary: The tenant-wide rule library and per-rule operations: list all rules, patch or delete one, run a test payload against one, and read aggregate rule stats.

nodes.summary: Reads and replaces the ordered set of rulesets a policy attaches, which is what determines evaluation order.

nodes.name: GET /manage/policies/{id}/flattened
nodes.summary: The merged, engine-ready view of a policy after its attached rulesets are flattened, including per-rule provenance.

nodes.name: GET /manage/policies/{id}/export
nodes.summary: Canonical policy YAML as text, for committing a policy to source control.

nodes.name: GET /manage/policies/{id}/versions
nodes.summary: The immutable policy version history: list versions, fetch or delete one, and publish a draft version to the engine.

nodes.name: GET /manage/detectors
nodes.summary: The detector catalogue the execution plan is built from.

nodes.name: GET /manage/models
nodes.summary: The ML model catalogue available to model-backed match kinds and detector stages.

nodes.name: GET /manage/api-keys
nodes.summary: API key CRUD and usage stats: list keys, create one (returning the one-time secret), patch, delete, and read per-key stats.

nodes.name: POST /manage/api-keys/{id}/revoke
nodes.summary: API key lifecycle transitions — revoke, suspend, reactivate and rotate (with an optional grace period).

nodes.name: PUT /manage/api-keys/{id}/classes
nodes.summary: Sets the agent classes a key belongs to (and the legacy single-class assignment), which is what resolves the key to a policy set.

nodes.name: POST /manage/guard/test
nodes.summary: Runs a sample payload through the guard pipeline and returns the decision and detections, backing the Guard Tester screen.

nodes.name: GET /manage/registry/classes
nodes.summary: Agent class registry CRUD: list, create, update, retire and delete classes, with the slug path-encoded.

nodes.name: GET /manage/registry/observed
nodes.summary: Agent classes the guard has observed in traffic but that are not yet registered.

nodes.name: GET /manage/registry/enforcement
nodes.summary: Reads and sets the registry enforcement mode, which decides what happens to traffic from unregistered classes.

nodes.name: GET /manage/audit
nodes.summary: The paginated audit trail with filter query params, plus the captured request payload for a single audit row.

nodes.name: GET /manage/audit/stats
nodes.summary: Aggregate audit counters and the hourly time series behind the dashboard charts.

nodes.name: POST /manage/feedback
nodes.summary: Submits analyst feedback against a request id and reads back the feedback already recorded for one.

nodes.name: GET /manage/stats/summary
nodes.summary: Windowed traffic and decision summary counters, and the reset that zeroes the in-memory counters.

nodes.name: GET /manage/auth/me
nodes.summary: Session identity and lifecycle: the caller's user and capabilities, server-side logout, and the unauthenticated SSO status probe the login screen calls before a token exists.

nodes.name: GET /manage/users
nodes.summary: Local user administration: list, create, patch, delete, activate, deactivate and change password. Every route is capability-enforced server-side.

nodes.name: GET /manage/authz/catalogue
nodes.summary: The server-generated role x capability catalogue, the single source of truth the capability matrix renders.

nodes.name: GET /manage/idp
nodes.summary: OIDC identity-provider configuration: read, update, and rotate the SCIM provisioning token.

nodes.name: GET /manage/receipts/export
nodes.summary: Receipt export for a query window, returned as a downloadable file body.

nodes.name: GET /platform/tenants
nodes.summary: Tenant administration on the `/platform` routes — siblings of `/manage`, not children — covering list, create, status change and key rotation.

nodes.name: GET /api/health
nodes.summary: Unauthenticated health and version probes, fetched bare rather than through the authenticated pipeline.

nodes.name: useAllRules
nodes.summary: Fans out one rules query per ruleset with `useQueries` and flattens the results, so the rule table can be built without an N+1 of manual effects.

nodes.name: useSetPolicyRulesets
nodes.summary: Mutation that replaces a policy's ordered ruleset attachment set and invalidates the attachment, flattened and ruleset-policies caches together.

nodes.name: useRulesByRuleset
nodes.summary: Parallel per-ruleset rule queries keyed by ruleset id, returning a map the flattened-policy view indexes into.

nodes.name: useThreats
nodes.summary: Loads recent audit entries and maps them to threat events, so the threat feed reads from the audit trail without knowing its wire shape.

nodes.name: useSsoStatus
nodes.summary: Queries SSO status for the login screen, tolerating the unauthenticated case rather than treating a failure as a session problem.

nodes.name: useSsoStatusFor
nodes.summary: SSO status for a named organisation, used when the login screen has an org hint to resolve before offering password entry.

nodes.name: mapAuditEntriesToThreats
nodes.summary: Maps audit entries to threat events, accepting both the current `{risk_score, items}` detections wrapper and the legacy bare array, and deriving a risk score from the highest detection confidence when the row has none stored.

nodes.name: can
nodes.summary: The capability predicate the whole UI gates on: true only when the capability is present, so an absent or unknown capability fails closed.

nodes.name: CapabilitiesProvider
nodes.summary: React context provider carrying the caller's capability set, seeded from `GET /manage/auth/me`.

nodes.name: useCapabilities
nodes.summary: Hook returning the current capability set and a bound `can()`, throwing outside the provider.

nodes.name: RequireCapability
nodes.summary: Render guard that shows its children only when the caller holds the named capability.

nodes.name: KpiCard.tsx
nodes.summary: The dense counter card the KPI strips are built from: localised tabular figure, optional delta chip, caption, sparkline slot, a pillar accent bar and a top-right pill slot.

nodes.name: Pill.tsx
nodes.summary: The pill primitive and its four domain-specific wrappers — ActionPill, SeverityPill, LiveRoadmapPill and DeltaBadge. The base component sets no colour itself; `data-tone` rules in the stylesheet do, which keeps the same verdict looking identical across every screen.

nodes.name: StackedBar.tsx
nodes.summary: Horizontal bar split by outcome, which doubles as a budget meter when an explicit `total` is passed and the remainder is left as visible track.
nodes.languageNotes: Meter and stacked bar are deliberately one component — a meter is a one-segment bar, and shipping two would give two sets of rounding and two empty states.

nodes.name: Stat.tsx
nodes.summary: A plain labelled figure with optional hint and VisualState emphasis; numbers are localised and rendered with tabular figures so columns line up.

nodes.name: StatusDot.tsx
nodes.summary: The default status treatment across the console: a ~6px coloured dot with an optional label beside it, coloured only through `visualStateColor`.
nodes.languageNotes: The label sits in its own `<span>` so Testing-Library text queries keep matching exactly when a page swaps a badge for a dot.

nodes.name: environment.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves which deployment the console is pointed at from an explicit override or the hostname, and maps that environment onto a VisualState. Unknown hosts deliberately resolve to production.

nodes.name: palette.ts
nodes.summary: The single module permitted to hold hex literals, mirroring the CSS custom properties for chart libraries that cannot resolve `var(--…)`. One accent at three weights plus semantic and text values.
nodes.languageNotes: Asserted against index.css by tokens.test.ts, while aesthetics.test.ts fails the build on a hex written anywhere else.

nodes.name: pillars.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the four top-level product pillars (activity, guardrails, developers, admin) used as accent keys; Overview is deliberately excluded because it aggregates all four.

nodes.name: visualState.ts
nodes.summary: The single source of truth for how domain facts become colour: a five-value VisualState vocabulary plus mappings for decision effects, lifecycles, severities, policy modes, API-key statuses and numeric risk scores. Screens import a mapping, never a colour.
nodes.languageNotes: Every mapper takes `string` rather than its own union, because callers hold server-typed values; an unrecognised input resolves to `neutral` so an unknown verdict is never invented as danger.

nodes.name: seriesWeight
nodes.summary: Computes the opacity for the nth of a set of donut segments, stepping from full accent down to about a third so ordered categories read as one hue at decreasing weight.

nodes.name: DonutChart
nodes.summary: Renders the donut as stacked SVG circles with computed stroke dash offsets, colouring each arc by its VisualState or, under `shadeBySeries`, by its position in the series.

nodes.name: EnvironmentBadge
nodes.summary: Resolves the current environment from the injected prop or the live hostname plus build env, hides itself on local when `whenNotable` is set, and renders the name behind a state-coloured dot.

nodes.name: HealthPill
nodes.summary: Renders the health signal as the console's only solid-filled pill, delegating layout and tone handling to the shared `Pill` primitive.

nodes.name: InForce
nodes.summary: Renders the published policy version, a 'never published' case when none is running, and a second line naming the newer draft only when one is genuinely ahead.

nodes.name: KpiCard
nodes.summary: Lays out the KPI card: pill slot, label, localised tabular value, optional sparkline and a delta-plus-caption context line, with the pillar accent applied through a data attribute.

nodes.name: Pill
nodes.summary: The base pill: composes the mono and solid class variants and emits `data-tone` so the stylesheet, not the component, decides the colour.

nodes.name: ActionPill
nodes.summary: Renders a firewall verdict (allow, flag, modify, block) as a monospace pill toned by the pinned effect mapping, so the same action is the same colour on every screen.

nodes.name: SeverityPill
nodes.summary: Renders a rule severity as a monospace pill whose tone comes from the shared severity mapping.

nodes.name: LiveRoadmapPill
nodes.summary: Labels a surface as Live, Roadmap or New so a screen the backend cannot yet populate says so instead of rendering an empty panel.

nodes.name: DeltaBadge
nodes.summary: The KPI delta chip, taking a VisualState so a delta and the figure above it are coloured from the same source.

nodes.name: StackedBar
nodes.summary: Drops zero-valued segments, computes each share against either the segment sum or an explicit total, and renders the result as a labelled accessible bar that stays honest when empty.

nodes.name: Stat
nodes.summary: Renders a labelled figure with tabular localised numbers, applying a VisualState colour only when emphasis was asked for.

nodes.name: StatusDot
nodes.summary: Renders an aria-hidden coloured dot plus an optional label span, taking its colour solely from `visualStateColor`.

nodes.name: resolveEnvironment
nodes.summary: Resolves the deployment environment from an explicit override, then loopback and `.local` hostname checks, then a staging/uat/qa pattern, defaulting anything unknown to production.
nodes.languageNotes: The fail-safe direction is deliberate: a production box that reads as local is the failure worth preventing, never the reverse.

nodes.name: environmentState
nodes.summary: Maps an environment onto a VisualState — local neutral, staging caution, production danger.

nodes.name: effectVisualState
nodes.summary: Maps a decision effect (allow, flag, modify, approve, block) onto a VisualState, falling back to neutral for anything unrecognised.

nodes.name: lifecycleVisualState
nodes.summary: Maps a registration lifecycle state (unregistered, pending, active, customized, retired) onto a VisualState, defaulting to neutral.

nodes.name: severityVisualState
nodes.summary: Maps a rule severity (info through critical) onto a VisualState, defaulting to neutral so an unknown severity is never shown as danger.

nodes.name: policyModeVisualState
nodes.summary: Maps a policy rollout mode (off, monitor, enforce) onto a VisualState; a deliberately disabled policy reads neutral rather than red.

nodes.name: apiKeyStatusVisualState
nodes.summary: Maps an API-key status (active, suspended, expired, revoked) onto a VisualState so a paused key is visibly different from a killed one.

nodes.name: riskVisualState
nodes.summary: Bands a 0..1 risk or confidence score onto the visual vocabulary at the pinned thresholds (>=0.8 danger, >=0.5 caution, otherwise neutral).

nodes.name: visualStateColor
nodes.summary: The only function in the app that turns a VisualState into a colour, resolving to a CSS custom property rather than a literal.

nodes.name: CommandPalette.tsx
nodes.summary: The Cmd-K command palette: a search input over the in-app user guide that scores the docs corpus on every keystroke and hands the chosen section to the slide-over panel rather than navigating away. Built as an ARIA combobox-over-listbox so the highlighted result is announced while the reader is still typing.
nodes.languageNotes: Hits carry a `kind` discriminant from the start so future non-doc actions can join the same result list without rewriting the palette around them.

nodes.name: DocsContent.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders one documentation section's body, splitting build-time Shiki code HTML (injected as markup) from prose (rendered through react-markdown with GFM). Internal /docs links are rewritten to React Router Link elements so they stay in-app.
nodes.languageNotes: Splitting code from markdown avoids a rehype-raw dependency: react-markdown escapes raw HTML, so pre-highlighted code embedded in markdown would render as literal angle brackets.

nodes.name: DocsPanel.tsx
nodes.summary: The docs slide-over: shows a single page or anchored section beside the working screen, which is never unmounted and so keeps its filters, selection and scroll position. Implements the same focus contract as ui/Modal - focus enters the panel and returns to the opener on Escape.
nodes.languageNotes: The onClose handler is held in a ref so the Escape listener effect does not re-subscribe on every parent render.

nodes.name: plainText.ts
nodes.summary: Strips markdown scaffolding from a docs section to produce the plain prose that search scoring and result snippets run against. Table separator rows are dropped, cell dividers become readable separators, link URLs are discarded in favour of their words, and code blocks are excluded entirely.
nodes.languageNotes: Derived in the browser rather than emitted into docs.json: shipping the plain text alongside the markdown duplicated the whole corpus for ~28 KB gzipped of content the client already had.

nodes.name: search.ts
nodes.summary: Full-text scoring over the docs corpus with no search library and no prebuilt index - every section is scored per keystroke, weighting title matches above headings above body text. Returns ranked Hit records carrying a snippet showing why each result matched.
nodes.languageNotes: At ~501 short sections the corpus is fast enough to be its own index, which keeps the feature dependency-free and fully offline.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Type contract for the documentation corpus - DocsCorpus, DocsPage, DocsSection and DocsBlock - describing exactly the shape that scripts/build-docs-index.mjs emits into the build-time-generated src/generated/docs.json.
nodes.languageNotes: The generator is plain JS and cannot import these types, so the two sides are kept in step by hand and a generator test is what catches a mismatch.

nodes.name: useDocs.ts
nodes.summary: React hook that lazily loads the bundled documentation corpus on first use and caches the promise at module scope, so the palette and the panel share one fetch per session. The payload is a dynamic import of the build-generated src/generated/docs.json, not a network call.
nodes.languageNotes: Bundled rather than fetched - the whole ~112 KB gzipped corpus ships with the app, which is why the docs work with no network at all.

nodes.name: Docs.tsx
nodes.summary: The /docs route: a full-page documentation reader showing a table of contents when no slug is given, and the whole page with anchor scrolling when one is. Deliberately the fallback surface - the slide-over panel is the primary one, and docs is not a seventh nav section.

nodes.name: CommandPalette
nodes.summary: Command palette component: memoises search results per query, tracks the highlighted index, and wires arrow/Enter/Escape keys plus mouse hover to selection. Picking a hit calls onPick with its target path and then closes.

nodes.name: DocsContent
nodes.summary: Maps a section's blocks to output: code blocks are injected as pre-highlighted HTML, markdown blocks go through react-markdown with a custom anchor renderer that turns internal /docs hrefs into router links.

nodes.name: DocsPanel
nodes.summary: Slide-over panel component: parses the /docs/<slug>#<anchor> target into page and section, narrows the page to the requested section when anchored, and manages Escape-to-close plus focus return to the opening element.

nodes.name: sectionText
nodes.summary: Reduces a DocsSection to searchable prose by joining its markdown blocks and running a documented chain of regex substitutions that remove table scaffolding, link URLs, repeated headings and markdown punctuation.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Scores every section of the corpus against the query terms using weighted title/heading/body matches, attaches a snippet around the first body match, and returns the top `limit` hits sorted by score.

nodes.name: useDocs
nodes.summary: Hook returning { corpus, loading }; triggers the shared lazy load on mount and guards the state update with a liveness flag so an unmounted consumer never sets state.

nodes.name: Docs
nodes.summary: Route component for /docs and /docs/*: resolves the slug from the wildcard param, scrolls to the URL hash once the page has loaded, and renders either the corpus table of contents or the full page with per-section anchors.

nodes.name: attention.ts
nodes.summary: Pure derivation layer that turns data the app has already fetched (API keys, rulesets, policies, users) into a ranked queue of AttentionItem objects - each carrying a severity, a one-word condition label, a headline, the consequence of ignoring it, and a verb plus route to the screen that fixes it. Defines the AttentionItem interface that the Home screen renders.
nodes.languageNotes: Severity and label are modelled as string literal unions rather than enums, so the pill tone mapping in the UI stays exhaustively checkable at compile time.

nodes.name: deriveAttentionQueue
nodes.summary: Takes optional arrays of keys, rulesets, policies and users and returns AttentionItem[] sorted by descending weight. Emits one item per API key expiring within 7 days (danger under 2 days, otherwise caution weighted 80 minus days left, with distinct copy for already-lapsed keys), one tenant-wide item for the first ruleset carrying a compile_error, one item when exactly one active admin remains, and one aggregate item when any policies have sync_status 'drifted'.

nodes.name: dates.ts
nodes.summary: Single-function date helper bridging the HTML5 datetime-local input, which emits naive local-clock strings, and the backend's chrono::DateTime<Utc> query params, which require full RFC 3339. Its header comment records why sending the naive string produces a 400 and why treating it as UTC would silently misread non-UTC users.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on the ES2017 rule that the Date constructor interprets a timezone-less date-time string as local time, so toISOString performs the local-to-UTC conversion for free.

nodes.name: localDatetimeToUtcIso
nodes.summary: Converts a local-clock datetime string to a UTC ISO 8601 string with a Z suffix. Returns an empty string for empty input and for anything the Date constructor cannot parse, so 'Invalid Date' never reaches a query param; values that already carry a timezone round-trip to the same instant, making the call idempotent.

nodes.name: ExportEvidence.tsx
nodes.summary: Modal dialog for downloading the server-computed signed evidence bundle - decision receipts plus the chain checkpoints that verify them - over a chosen date range. Distinct from the audit page's Export JSON/CSV, which only serialise the rows currently on screen.

nodes.name: ExportEvidence
nodes.summary: Default-exported modal component seeded with the server's own default window (today back seven days). Validates that the start date is not after the end date, widens the day-granularity inputs to T00:00 and T23:59:59 before normalising them through localDatetimeToUtcIso, calls exportReceipts, and saves the JSON response via an object-URL anchor click named sif-evidence-<from>-<to>.json.

nodes.name: useStatsSummary.ts
nodes.summary: The client-side single source of truth for headline request counters, so every page showing totals for the same window renders identical numbers. Defines an all-zero EMPTY_SUMMARY fallback and the polling options interface.

nodes.name: useStatsSummary
nodes.summary: TanStack Query hook keyed on ['stats-summary', windowHours] that calls getStatsSummary on a refetchInterval (default 10s, overridable and disableable). Returns the legacy shape {summary, loading, error, refresh}, substituting EMPTY_SUMMARY while data is undefined so a background refetch never blanks the counters, and flattening the error to a string or null.
nodes.languageNotes: Two mounted consumers share one cache entry, so the shared query key is what stops the page polling the endpoint twice.

nodes.name: AuditLog.tsx
nodes.summary: The audit trail screen: nine URL-seeded text filters plus a degraded-only toggle over a paginated entry table, a URL-addressable detail pane, client-side JSON and CSV export of the rows on screen, the signed-evidence export dialog, and the AuditLedger panel. Hoists the Event Type option list so the 'is this a value we know?' test is derived from it rather than duplicated.
nodes.languageNotes: TEXT_FILTER_KEYS is declared `as const` and the Filters type is derived from it, so adding a filter key updates the record type, the URL seeding loop and the chip list in one edit.

nodes.name: AuditLog
nodes.summary: Default-exported page component. Seeds its filter state once from the URL search params so other screens can deep-link into a slice of the trail, derives the selected entry from ?id=, normalises date filters through localDatetimeToUtcIso, and reduces a pasted full API key to the public prefix the trail actually stores before querying audit entries, stats and keys.

nodes.name: Home.tsx
nodes.summary: The landing screen, built as an attention queue rather than a dashboard: a greeting by name and time of day, the derived items that need a person each with a routing verb, then four KPI cards with hourly sparklines. Holds the greeting helpers, the spelled-number list and the severity-to-chip-class map.

nodes.name: currentUsername
nodes.summary: Reads the username out of the sif_user blob App.tsx persists from /manage/auth/me in localStorage, returning null for a missing, empty or unparseable value so the greeting drops the name rather than inventing one.

nodes.name: Home
nodes.summary: Default-exported page component. Gates each source query on the caller's capability (keys and users are only fetched with apikey:read / user:read so viewers do not meet a permission banner on their landing screen), feeds the results to deriveAttentionQueue, and renders the queue alongside KPI cards whose block rate, sparklines and half-over-half delta come from the selected period's stats summary and the last 24 hourly buckets.

nodes.name: Button.tsx
nodes.summary: Defines the console's single button primitive: a thin wrapper over the native `<button>` whose only added prop is a `variant` token (primary, secondary, ghost, danger) that resolves to a `btn-*` class rather than any colour value. Its doc comment records the capability-gating convention used across the app — a disabled button plus a `title` explaining why, with the server remaining the only real enforcement point.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends `ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>` and spreads `...rest`, so every native button attribute passes straight through. The `variant` default is `secondary`, not `primary` — the design permits one filled action per screen, so the outline style has to be the one you get for free.

nodes.name: Button
nodes.summary: Renders a `<button>` with `type="button"` by default and a class list built from the `variant` token plus any caller `className`. Carries no colour of its own — the variant name is the whole styling contract.

nodes.name: DirtyBar.tsx
nodes.summary: Sticky unsaved-changes bar that names the changed fields in prose ("2 unsaved changes — retries and timeout. Nothing runs until you save.") and puts Discard beside the commit action. Its inline styles reach for CSS custom properties such as `--ac-wash`, `--ac-line` and `--fg` rather than literal colours, keeping it inside the rule that only `src/ui/palette.ts` may hold hex values.
nodes.languageNotes: Renders `null` when `changes` is empty, so callers can mount it unconditionally. `role="status"` makes the change list a polite live region for screen readers.

nodes.name: DirtyBar
nodes.summary: Builds a readable list from the `changes` field names and renders it beside ghost Discard and primary Save buttons, swapping the save label for "Saving…" while `busy` is set. Returns null when there is nothing dirty.

nodes.name: Pager.tsx
nodes.summary: The footer of every paged table: a "Showing 1–8 of 8 keys" count, a per-page Select fed from `PAGE_SIZES`, and Previous/Next ghost buttons around a stated "Page 1 of 3". It deliberately renders even for a single page — a control that only appears past a threshold is one nobody knows exists — and hides only when the list is genuinely empty.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic over the row type `T` purely to accept `Pagination<T>` from `usePager`; it never touches a row. Numbered page links were rejected on purpose because these tables are searched and filtered rather than browsed.

nodes.name: Pager
nodes.summary: Destructures a `Pagination<T>` object and renders the count line, the page-size Select, and the two step buttons, disabling each at its end of the range. Returns null when `total` is zero.

nodes.name: PanelStatus.tsx
nodes.summary: Decides the loading / error / empty / data tri-state once for every panel instead of nine times, taking the `{loading, error, data}` shape the app's TanStack Query hooks produce and calling the children render-prop only when there is something to show. Error is checked before empty on purpose: a failed fetch leaves `data` at its initial empty value, and reporting that as "no data yet" would turn an outage into a shrug.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic over the payload type `T` with `children` and `empty` as render-prop callbacks, so the panel body never renders against a half-loaded value. The loading branch pairs an `aria-hidden` skeleton with an `sr-only` "Loading" so both audiences get a signal; status styling comes from `panel-state-*` classes, not inline colour.

nodes.name: PanelStatus
nodes.summary: Short-circuits in order — skeleton while loading, `role="alert"` message with an optional Retry button on error, `emptyMessage` when the caller's `empty` predicate matches — and otherwise renders `children(data)`.

nodes.name: Select.tsx
nodes.summary: The console's one dropdown: an APG select-only combobox that replaces the native `<select>`, whose popup is drawn by the operating system and so cannot be styled by the app's stylesheet. Supports type-to-narrow search past eight options, grouped rows with hints, a clear affordance, an optional footer action, and a hidden input so a plain uncontrolled form still reads the value from `FormData`.
nodes.languageNotes: The popup is `position: fixed` and placed by measurement because the console nests `overflow: hidden` panels inside `overflow-x: auto` table scrollers, either of which would clip an absolutely-positioned menu. Focus never leaves the trigger or the search box — `aria-activedescendant` moves instead — and the listbox suppresses the `mousedown` default so pressing a row cannot blur the control and unmount the row mid-press. The file carries unusually long comments recording the browser behaviour behind each of those decisions.

nodes.name: Select
nodes.summary: Implements the whole combobox: open/query/highlight state, a memoised filter over label, hint and group, outside-mousedown and focusout close handlers, viewport measurement that flips the popup upwards only when below genuinely cannot hold it, and arrow/Enter/Escape/Tab key handling that skips disabled rows. Opening lands the highlight on the current choice rather than row zero.

nodes.name: usePager.ts
nodes.summary: The pagination hook behind every paged table, plus the `PAGE_SIZES` (25/50/100) and `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` constants and the `Pagination<T>` shape that `Pager` renders. The smallest size is the default on purpose — the hook exists because long lists pushed bulk actions off the bottom of the screen.
nodes.languageNotes: `PAGE_SIZES` is `as const` and `PageSize` is derived from it, so the size union and the offered options can never drift apart. The current page is clamped on every render rather than stored, because an effect that writes the state it reads is how render loops start.

nodes.name: usePager
nodes.summary: Slices a filtered row list into pages, resetting to page one when the caller's `resetKey` (a string digest of its filters) or the page size changes, and clamping the requested page into range so a list that shrinks under an open page shows its last page rather than nothing. Returns the rows plus one-based display bounds.

nodes.name: endpoints.ts
nodes.summary: Codewall's own API module for enrolled endpoints: the Endpoint record type, list/query parameter types, and two thin wrappers over the shared request helper for GET /manage/endpoints. Kept out of the shared src/api layer because the endpoint surface belongs only to the Codewall product build.
nodes.languageNotes: Types are declared as interfaces with literal unions (state: 'active' | 'revoked'), so the compiler carries the server's enum vocabulary rather than a bare string.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Vite HTML entry document for the Codewall product build: sets the Codewall Control Plane title and shield favicon, and mounts the app into #root via ./main.tsx.
nodes.languageNotes: One of two per-product HTML entries; Vite is pointed at this directory with --mode codewall, which is what makes one src/ tree build into two differently-branded apps.

nodes.name: Endpoints.tsx
nodes.summary: The Codewall-only Endpoints screen: a paged, capability-gated table of enrolled endpoints showing hostname, agent, policy version, last-seen time and a status dot derived from revocation and receipt-gap state.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads its data through TanStack Query with enabled tied to the endpoint:manage capability, so an unauthorised viewer never fires the request at all.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Vite HTML entry document for the SIF product build: sets the Semantic Intercept Firewall title and shield favicon, and mounts the app into #root via ./main.tsx.

nodes.name: eslint.config.js
nodes.summary: Flat ESLint configuration for the dashboard: TypeScript plus the classic react-hooks guarantees everywhere, with the react-hooks v7 compiler-verified rules turned on only for the migrated surface (pages, the query layer, the polling hooks) and explicitly off elsewhere.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the flat-config array form with per-glob override blocks, which is how the file expresses a staged migration: the stricter rules are scoped to the directories that have already left the fetch-in-effect pattern.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Package manifest for semanticd-dashboard. Its scripts encode the two-product build: every dev, build, test and typecheck task exists twice, once with --mode sif and once with --mode codewall, each preceded by the docs-index generation step.
nodes.languageNotes: Leans on npm's pre* lifecycle hooks (prebuild, pretest, pretypecheck) so the generated docs index is always fresh before any task that consumes it.

nodes.name: build-docs-index.mjs
nodes.summary: Build-time generator that walks docs/user-guide, splits each page into sections, syntax-highlights fenced code with Shiki, resolves cross-links to page slugs and heading anchors, and emits src/generated/docs.json for the in-app user guide and command palette.
nodes.languageNotes: Highlighting runs in Node at build time so the browser ships no Shiki. The module only writes its output when invoked directly (import.meta.url compared against argv[1]), which lets tests import buildCorpus without the import having a file-writing side effect.

nodes.name: verify-product-build.mjs
nodes.summary: Post-build guard that asserts the product boundary held: it reads dist/manifest.json and the emitted bundles to confirm the shared dashboard is present, the expected product title is baked in, and the Codewall endpoint surface appears in the Codewall build and only there.
nodes.languageNotes: A top-level-await ESM script that throws on failure, so the npm script's non-zero exit is the whole reporting mechanism.

nodes.name: index.css
nodes.summary: The console's single global stylesheet and design-token layer: CSS custom properties for surfaces, text, the one accent, semantic state colours, radii and elevation, a dark-theme override block, and the full component vocabulary (nav, cards, tables, pills, KPI strips, charts, modals, responsive rules).
nodes.languageNotes: Tokens are plain CSS custom properties on :root with a dark override, so theming needs no framework. The comments record measured contrast ratios and the reasoning behind each choice, making the file as much a design document as a stylesheet.

nodes.name: AreaTimeline.tsx
nodes.summary: A hand-drawn filled area chart over time with an optional lighter comparison series, replacing the previous recharts-based timeline so the console ships no chart library.
nodes.languageNotes: Draws in a fixed 100xH user space with preserveAspectRatio='none', so CSS sizes it and no ResizeObserver or measurement pass is needed. Gradient ids come from useId to keep multiple instances on a page from colliding.

nodes.name: Card.tsx
nodes.summary: The console's container primitive: a hairline border and whitespace, with an optional uppercase eyebrow title and a right-aligned actions slot on the title row.

nodes.name: EmptyState.tsx
nodes.summary: The muted, centred block every page shows for loading and empty-list states, so only the wording varies between screens and never the treatment.

nodes.name: ErrorBanner.tsx
nodes.summary: Dismissible page-level error banner carrying the server's own message, a single shared copy of markup that individual pages used to inline.
nodes.languageNotes: Carries role='alert' so the message is announced when it appears rather than only being visible.

nodes.name: Field.tsx
nodes.summary: A labelled form control wrapper with an optional hint line, associating the label either by htmlFor when the control carries its own id or by wrapping when it does not.
nodes.languageNotes: Both association modes keep getByLabelText working, which is what lets the test suite query fields uniformly across pages that build forms differently.

nodes.name: KpiStrip.tsx
nodes.summary: The row of counters that sits directly under a page header, one half of the console's page composition pattern of header plus KPI strip plus panels.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps its children in role='group' with a caller-supplied aria-label, so the strip is announced as one named region rather than a run of loose numbers.

nodes.name: Modal.tsx
nodes.summary: The console's dialog shell: an overlay plus card that traps Tab focus inside itself, closes on Escape or backdrop click, moves focus to the first focusable element on open, and returns it to the opener on close.
nodes.languageNotes: Holds the close callback in a ref so the key handler effect does not re-subscribe on every render while still calling the latest callback.

nodes.name: PeriodSwitcher.tsx
nodes.summary: The shared time-range segmented control, exporting the period vocabulary (PERIODS, PERIOD_HOURS, PERIOD_LABEL) alongside the component so every screen agrees on what each range means in hours.

nodes.name: Sparkline.tsx
nodes.summary: Two inline micro-charts for KPI cards: Sparkline draws a normalised polyline over a value series, BarSparkline draws the same data as proportional bars.

nodes.name: Tooltip.tsx
nodes.summary: The console's own tooltip, opening on hover and on focus, used deliberately in place of the native title attribute so that prose taken off a crowded screen stays findable and styleable.
nodes.languageNotes: Generates its describedby id with useId and opens on focus as well as hover, since a keyboard user cannot hover and a native title would never appear for them at all.

nodes.name: icons.tsx
nodes.summary: The four inline SVG row verbs (move up, move down, delete, drag grip) shared by any panel with reorderable rows, replacing per-row spelled-out sentences that forced every row to wrap.
nodes.languageNotes: The icons carry no text of their own by design: callers supply the full phrase as aria-label, so the wording moves to assistive technology rather than being deleted.

nodes.name: useRowDrag.ts
nodes.summary: Hook implementing drag-to-reorder for row lists, returning grip props for the drag source, row props for every drop target, the in-flight indices, and the drop-edge class marking where the dragged row would actually land.
nodes.languageNotes: The grip rather than the row is the drag source, because rows contain links and links are natively draggable. Drag is always offered alongside keyboard move-earlier/move-later buttons, never as the only affordance.

nodes.name: useScrollToTop.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that puts a newly-opened route at the top of the window, keying on pathname only so in-page query state does not yank the reader's place, and standing aside when the URL carries a hash.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately not React Router's ScrollRestoration, which belongs to the data routers; this app mounts useRoutes under a plain BrowserRouter.

nodes.name: vite-env.d.ts
nodes.summary: Single-line ambient type reference pulling in vite/client, which gives the source tree types for import.meta.env and Vite's asset imports.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript compiler configuration for the dashboard: strict mode with noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters, bundler module resolution, the react-jsx transform, noEmit, and the @/* path alias onto src/. Covers both the shared src tree and the per-product apps directory.

nodes.name: vite.config.ts
nodes.summary: Shared Vite configuration for both product builds: the /dashboard/ base path, the React plugin, the @ alias, a manifest-emitting dist build, the Vitest jsdom setup, and a dev proxy forwarding /api, /manage, /platform and /ws to the manage service on port 8081.

nodes.name: listEndpoints
nodes.summary: Builds a query string from the supplied list parameters and fetches the paged endpoint list from GET /manage/endpoints.

nodes.name: getEndpoint
nodes.summary: Fetches a single endpoint by id, URL-encoding the identifier before it reaches the path.

nodes.name: Endpoints
nodes.summary: The Endpoints page component: checks the endpoint:manage capability, runs the paged endpoints query, keeps page size and offset in state, and renders the table with per-row status dots plus paging and panel status.

nodes.name: anchorOf
nodes.summary: Turns a heading string into the slugified anchor id the rendered docs page will use.

nodes.name: headingsOf
nodes.summary: Returns the set of section anchors defined in a markdown file, memoised per file so repeated cross-link checks do not re-read the same page.

nodes.name: resolveLink
nodes.summary: Resolves a relative markdown cross-link into the in-app page slug and fragment, leaving absolute and external URLs alone and reporting fragments that name no existing heading.

nodes.name: toBlocks
nodes.summary: Splits a section body into an ordered list of markdown and pre-highlighted code blocks, keeping trusted HTML separate from the text react-markdown will escape.

nodes.name: buildCorpus
nodes.summary: Builds the whole docs corpus: creates the Shiki highlighter, walks every markdown page into sections and blocks, resolves cross-links, and throws if any fragment points at a heading that no longer exists.

nodes.name: AreaTimeline
nodes.summary: Renders the filled area path, optional comparison line and first/last axis labels for a time series, dropping a comparison series whose length does not match rather than drawing it against the wrong buckets.

nodes.name: Card
nodes.summary: Renders the card container, adding the title row with its eyebrow and actions slot only when a title is supplied.

nodes.name: EmptyState
nodes.summary: Renders the shared muted, centred block used for loading and empty-list messages.

nodes.name: ErrorBanner
nodes.summary: Renders the dismissible error alert with the server's message and a dismiss control.

nodes.name: Field
nodes.summary: Renders a label, its control and an optional hint, associating label and control by htmlFor or by wrapping.

nodes.name: KpiStrip
nodes.summary: Wraps KPI cards in the responsive grid and names the row as an accessible group.

nodes.name: Modal
nodes.summary: Renders the dialog overlay and card, wires Escape and backdrop dismissal, cycles Tab within the dialog, and restores focus to the opener when it unmounts.

nodes.name: PeriodSwitcher
nodes.summary: Renders the segmented time-range control, marking the selected period and reporting changes to the caller.

nodes.name: Sparkline
nodes.summary: Draws a value series as a normalised polyline inside a fixed-size inline SVG, scaling to the series' own min and max.

nodes.name: BarSparkline
nodes.summary: Draws the same value series as proportional bars, each sized against the largest value in the set.

nodes.name: Tooltip
nodes.summary: Wraps its trigger with hover and focus handlers, showing the tooltip bubble and linking it to the trigger by a generated id.

nodes.name: ArrowUp
nodes.summary: Inline SVG up arrow marking the move-earlier verb on a reorderable row.

nodes.name: ArrowDown
nodes.summary: Inline SVG down arrow marking the move-later verb on a reorderable row.

nodes.name: Trash
nodes.summary: Inline SVG bin icon marking the remove verb on a row.

nodes.name: Grip
nodes.summary: Inline SVG drag handle drawn as the grip that useRowDrag treats as the drag source.

nodes.name: useRowDrag
nodes.summary: Tracks the dragged and hovered row indices and returns the grip props, row drop-target props and drop-edge class, calling the caller's onReorder when a drop lands on a different row.

nodes.name: useScrollToTop
nodes.summary: Scrolls the window to the top whenever the route pathname changes, skipping the scroll entirely when the URL carries a hash anchor.

nodes.name: useRulesets
nodes.summary: Lists every ruleset under the shared `rulesetKeys.all` cache key — the entry point every rule and policy screen reads its ruleset roster from.

nodes.name: useRules
nodes.summary: Rules for one ruleset, gated on the id being present so the query stays idle until a ruleset is selected rather than firing against an empty path.

nodes.name: useRuleLibrary
nodes.summary: The whole cross-ruleset rule library under a single `ruleLibraryKey`, backing the rule picker's search over every rule regardless of which ruleset holds it.

nodes.name: useRuleStats
nodes.summary: Rule counts by category with a zeroed `placeholderData`, so the stats strip renders its shape immediately instead of collapsing while the first fetch is in flight.

nodes.name: useHealth
nodes.summary: Backend health under the `health` key — the same cache entry `useResetStats` invalidates, so a counter reset shows up without a page reload.

nodes.name: usePolicies
nodes.summary: The active policy list, archived entries excluded: an archived policy is not something to attach a class to or run a test through.

nodes.name: usePoliciesIncludingArchived
nodes.summary: The policy list with archived entries included, for the management screen where an archived policy still holds its name and a refused create over that name is only explicable if the holder can be seen (issue 263). Keyed under `["policies", …]` so the shared policy invalidation refetches it too.

nodes.name: usePolicyRulesets
nodes.summary: The ordered rulesets attached to one policy, keyed through `policyKeys.rulesets` and disabled until a policy id exists.

nodes.name: usePolicyFlattened
nodes.summary: What a policy's attached rulesets add up to — the server's flatten, in one request. The only answer that accounts for the merge: summing the per-ruleset lists double-counts every rule id that more than one ruleset names.

nodes.name: useRulesetPolicies
nodes.summary: The policies a given ruleset is attached to — the reverse-dependency view that shows what editing or detaching a ruleset would reach.

nodes.name: useResetStats
nodes.summary: Mutation that resets the server's request counters and invalidates `health` on settle, so the KPI strip reflects the reset without a reload.

nodes.name: useAuditStats
nodes.summary: Aggregate audit counters under the `audit-stats` key, backing the decision-mix totals on the landing and audit screens.

nodes.name: useDetectors
nodes.summary: The detector roster the rule editors and the Detectors screen read; also the source `useMlDetectorIds` narrows to classifier ids.

nodes.name: useModels
nodes.summary: Lists model ARTEFACTS from `models/manifest.json` — not the detector ids a rule's `model` field binds to. A rule authored from this menu bound to no detector and never fired; `useMlDetectorIds` answers the binding question instead (issue 311).

nodes.name: useMlDetectorIds
nodes.summary: The classifier detector ids an `ml_model` rule's `model` field may legitimately name, narrowed from `useDetectors`. Returns `undefined` while loading, if refused, or from a server too old to send the field — `RuleEditor` reads that as NOT ASKED and falls back to a text box, because an empty menu would leave an operator no way to author the rule at all.

nodes.name: useApiKeys
nodes.summary: The API key roster, with an `enabled` gate for callers that only WANT the keys — the audit filter's suggestion list, say. A caller without `apikey:read` asking anyway earns a 403 and the permission notice that comes with it, for a convenience the screen works fine without.

nodes.name: useAgentClasses
nodes.summary: The registered agent classes, under the `agent-classes` key that `useAgentClassInvalidation` refreshes.

nodes.name: useObservedClasses
nodes.summary: The discovery feed: agent classes seen in live traffic, including ones never registered — the input to unclassed-key triage.

nodes.name: useEnforcement
nodes.summary: The fleet-wide enforcement posture, read by the enforcement strip to show what each class currently resolves through.

nodes.name: useAgentClassInvalidation
nodes.summary: Returns a callback that invalidates both `agent-classes` and `api-keys`: changing a class's policy changes what every key in it resolves through, so leaving the key list alone would keep Fleet › Keys showing the old tier until a refresh.

nodes.name: useKeyInvalidation
nodes.summary: Returns a callback that invalidates the key list and the by-status counters together, so the KPI strip and the table never disagree after a create, delete or rotate.

nodes.name: useApiKeyStats
nodes.summary: By-status API key counters behind the same `enabled` gate as `useApiKeys`, feeding the KPI strip that `useKeyInvalidation` keeps in step with the table.

nodes.name: useIdpConfig
nodes.summary: The identity-provider configuration under `idp-config` — the cache entry both IdP mutations invalidate on settle.

nodes.name: useUpdateIdpConfig
nodes.summary: Mutation that writes the IdP configuration and invalidates `idp-config` on settle, so the form re-reads the server's accepted state rather than trusting its own optimistic copy.

nodes.name: useRotateScimToken
nodes.summary: Mutation that rotates the SCIM provisioning token and invalidates `idp-config`, surfacing the new token through the same read path as the rest of the IdP settings.

nodes.name: useUsers
nodes.summary: The user roster, gated by `enabled` because `GET /manage/users` requires `user:read`, which only admin and platform hold. A query armed for a caller the server will refuse spends a 403 on the permission banner for data it then discards.

nodes.name: useCapabilityCatalogue
nodes.summary: The capability catalogue backing the access-control screen's role and permission matrix.

nodes.name: useAuditEntries
nodes.summary: Audit entries for an arbitrary filter map, with the params folded into the query key so each distinct filter is its own cache entry rather than clobbering the last one.

nodes.name: useCapturedPayload
nodes.summary: The captured request payload for one audit entry, doubly gated on the caller's `enabled` flag and the request id being present, so opening the threat drawer fetches a body only when it is actually going to be shown.

nodes.name: useHourlyStats
nodes.summary: Hourly request buckets under the `hourly-stats` key — the series the threat timeline and the landing sparkline both draw from.

nodes.name: useTenants
nodes.summary: The tenant roster for the platform-level tenants screen.

nodes.name: getStatsSummary
nodes.summary: Fetches the windowed request and latency summary from `GET /manage/stats/summary`. The single upstream behind `useStatsSummary`, which every page showing headline counters reads through so the same window renders identical numbers everywhere.
